claims.title: Does FSD (Supervised) make my car autonomous?
claims.establishes: Tesla requires active supervision when using the customer feature.
claims.limits: It does not replace the driver.
claims.next: Check the owner’s manual for the actual vehicle and software.

claims.title: If a market is listed, does every Tesla get the feature?
claims.answer: A market listing is not an individual entitlement.
claims.establishes: Tesla describes availability as dependent on hardware, software, configuration and region.
claims.limits: A headline or country listing does not confirm installation on your car.
claims.next: Use the regional tracker, then check your exact car and Tesla’s local guidance.

claims.title: Does a country announcement confirm a customer rollout?
claims.answer: Permission and delivery need separate evidence.
claims.establishes: A country record can establish the action described by its underlying source.
claims.limits: A national announcement alone does not establish a particular customer installation or an EU-wide permission.
claims.next: Open the country record and look for distinct legal, listing and delivery evidence.

claims.title: Does Texas authorisation mean I can book a ride?
claims.answer: Legal status and service availability are different.
claims.establishes: Texas requires authorisation for commercial automated-vehicle operation.
claims.limits: A valid operator record alone does not establish a current booking in your neighbourhood.
claims.next: Check operator status separately from Tesla’s rider app.

claims.title: Does a California testing permit mean paid driverless rides?
claims.answer: Read the permit category, then the passenger-service record.
claims.establishes: DMV separates testing with a driver, driverless testing and deployment. CPUC publishes passenger-service permits separately.
claims.limits: One permission should not be presented as all of these permissions.
claims.next: Match the legal operator, category, conditions and record date.

claims.title: Are registered Cybercabs the number operating now?
claims.answer: A registration is not a car in service.
claims.establishes: A dated registry count describes vehicles listed in the source record.
claims.limits: It does not identify how many are available, carrying passengers or in a particular city at this moment.
claims.next: Keep registrations, observations and active-service evidence as separate measures.

claims.title: Does a Robotaxi ride prove Cybercab is operating there?
claims.answer: Identify the vehicle, not just the service name.
claims.establishes: Robotaxi is a service; a vehicle observation has a specific model and place.
claims.limits: A ride in one vehicle type does not establish availability of another.
claims.next: Use vehicle-specific records in the Cybercab tracker.

claims.title: Does “available in a city” mean every address?
claims.answer: The service boundary is narrower than the city name.
claims.establishes: Tesla describes limited service areas and shows them in its app.
claims.limits: A city label is not a guarantee for every pickup, destination or time.
claims.next: Check the app for the actual trip.

claims.title: Can a successful driverless clip prove all-road autonomy?
claims.answer: A clip documents a scenario. It cannot test every condition.
claims.establishes: An observation can show a task under the conditions captured.
claims.limits: It does not establish performance outside those conditions, undisclosed assistance or an unrestricted operating domain.
claims.next: Ask where the system can operate, what fallback it uses and what was independently observed.

claims.title: Do all “zero injuries” headlines count the same thing?
claims.answer: Read the endpoint before reading the zero.
claims.establishes: Tesla’s published injury measure uses a first-contact condition. Its own-airbag measure differs from any-vehicle airbag deployment.
claims.limits: Those definitions are not interchangeable with every injury allegation or deployment in SGO narratives.
claims.next: Read Tesla’s methodology alongside the regulator’s report definitions.

claims.title: Can raw crash totals tell us which system is safer?
claims.answer: Counts need exposure and matching definitions.
claims.establishes: A report can document a reported event under its reporting rules.
claims.limits: NHTSA totals are not normalized for miles, operating conditions or fleet exposure.
claims.next: Check the reporting population, miles and endpoint before comparing rates.

claims.title: Does zero observed mean zero risk?
claims.answer: No. A finite sample still leaves uncertainty.
claims.establishes: Zero qualifying events is an observation about a defined sample.
claims.limits: It is not proof that the underlying event rate is zero.
claims.next: Explore the illustrative model in the Safety lab.
